prompts.display_text: Pin a country or territory where ground was broken for a new temple in 2021.
prompts.text_original: Pin a country or territory where ground was broken for a new temple in 2021.
prompts.citation: ChurchofJesusChristTemples.org chronology and milestones, read 27 Oct 2026
prompts.summary: A groundbreaking starts construction of a temple, usually a few years after it is announced. 12 temple groundbreakings were held in 2021 in 7 countries or territories; see each answer for the temple and date.

answers.name: United States of America
answers.fact: Deseret Peak Utah (15 May 2021); Tallahassee Florida (5 June 2021); Syracuse Utah (12 June 2021); and 3 more.

answers.name: Brazil
answers.fact: Salvador Brazil (7 August 2021).

answers.name: Philippines
answers.fact: Bacolod Philippines (11 December 2021).

answers.name: Tonga
answers.fact: Neiafu Tonga (11 September 2021).

answers.name: Kenya
answers.fact: Nairobi Kenya (11 September 2021).

answers.name: American Samoa
answers.fact: Pago Pago American Samoa (30 October 2021).

answers.name: Cambodia
answers.fact: Phnom Penh Cambodia (18 September 2021).

prompts.display_text: Pin a Central American country an Apostle dedicated or rededicated for preaching from 1990 to 1992
prompts.text_original: Spencer W. Kimball dedicated all of Central America in 1952. Between 1990 and 1992 Apostles returned and dedicated (or, in one case, rededicated) each Central American country individually for the preaching of the gospel. A Central American country dedicated in that period.
prompts.summary: Elder Spencer W. Kimball dedicated Central America as a whole in 1952. In a burst from 1990 to 1992, Russell M. Nelson, Richard G. Scott, Howard W. Hunter, Marvin J. Ashton and Boyd K. Packer offered prayers for each country in turn, so every Central American nation received its own dedication.

answers.name: Guatemala
answers.fact: Rededicated by Marvin J. Ashton, October 19, 1991, in Quetzaltenango.

answers.name: Costa Rica
answers.fact: Boyd K. Packer, August 22, 1992.

answers.name: Honduras
answers.fact: Russell M. Nelson, June 1, 1991, on El Picacho above Tegucigalpa.

answers.name: El Salvador
answers.fact: Russell M. Nelson, April 7, 1990, in San Salvador.

answers.name: Nicaragua
answers.fact: Richard G. Scott and Russell M. Nelson, April 9, 1990, in Managua.

answers.name: Panama
answers.fact: Howard W. Hunter, August 24, 1991.

answers.name: Belize
answers.fact: Russell M. Nelson, June 23, 1991, with about 36 members present.

prompts.display_text: Pin a country whose very first stake of the Church was organized between 1995 and 1997
prompts.text_original: In just three years, 1995 to 1997, the Church organized first stakes in countries as far apart as Ireland, Thailand, Kiribati and Haiti. A country whose very first stake of the Church was organized between 1995 and 1997.
prompts.citation: Global Histories chronologies (Ireland, Singapore, Thailand, Papua New Guinea, Kiribati, DR Congo, Cote d'Ivoire, Haiti)
prompts.note: Ireland counts: Dublin's 1995 stake was its first. Belfast's 1974 stake is in the United Kingdom.
prompts.summary: In 1995 the Church organized first stakes in Singapore, Dublin, Bangkok and Port Moresby. Kiribati and Zaire, now DR Congo, followed in 1996, and Cote d'Ivoire and Haiti in 1997, showing how quickly the Church was maturing in Asia, the Pacific, Africa and the Caribbean.

answers.name: Ireland
answers.fact: The Dublin Ireland Stake, the first in the Republic of Ireland, was organized March 12, 1995.

answers.name: DR Congo
answers.fact: The Zaire Kinshasa Stake, the first in the country, was organized November 3, 1996.

answers.name: Haiti
answers.fact: The Port-au-Prince Haiti Stake, the first in Haiti, was organized September 21, 1997.

answers.name: Papua New Guinea
answers.fact: The Port Moresby Papua New Guinea Stake was created October 22, 1995, with Vaiba Rome as president.

answers.name: Singapore
answers.fact: The Singapore Stake was organized February 26, 1995, with Leonard Woo as president.

answers.name: Thailand
answers.fact: Elder Neal A. Maxwell created the Bangkok Thailand Stake, June 18-19, 1995.

answers.name: Cote d'Ivoire
answers.fact: The Abidjan Cote d'Ivoire Stake, the country's first, was organized August 17, 1997.

answers.name: Kiribati
answers.fact: Elder L. Tom Perry organized the Tarawa Kiribati Stake, August 11, 1996.

prompts.display_text: Pin a country whose modern name, or its main word, appears as a land, river or people in the King James New Testament
prompts.text_original: A present-day country whose name, or the main word of it, is spelled as a land, river or people in the King James New Testament
prompts.note: This prompt is about the name only, so Malta (Melita) and Romania (Romans) do not count.
prompts.summary: A dozen modern countries carry a name the King James New Testament already uses. Egypt, Israel, Syria, Greece, Italy and Cyprus are familiar, and the nation of Jordan takes its name from the river. Arabia, Macedonia, the Ethiopians, Libya and Spain also appear, the last as the place Paul hoped to reach after Rome.

answers.name: Egypt
answers.fact: Joseph was told to flee into Egypt (Matthew 2:13).

answers.name: Israel
answers.fact: Joseph was told to go into the land of Israel (Matthew 2:20).

answers.name: Greece
answers.fact: Paul came into Greece and stayed three months (Acts 20:2-3).

answers.name: Italy
answers.fact: It was determined that Paul should sail into Italy (Acts 27:1).

answers.name: Syria
answers.fact: Jesus' fame went throughout all Syria (Matthew 4:24).

answers.name: Cyprus
answers.fact: Barnabas was a Levite of the country of Cyprus (Acts 4:36).

answers.name: Jordan
answers.fact: John baptized in Jordan; the country takes its name from the river (Matthew 3:6).

answers.name: Ethiopia
answers.fact: Philip met a eunuch of great authority under Candace, queen of the Ethiopians (Acts 8:27).

answers.name: North Macedonia
answers.fact: Paul saw a man of Macedonia in a vision (Acts 16:9).

answers.name: Saudi Arabia
answers.fact: Paul went into Arabia after his conversion; Arabians heard at Pentecost (Galatians 1:17; Acts 2:11).

answers.name: Spain
answers.fact: Paul hoped to visit the Romans whenever he took his journey into Spain (Romans 15:24).

answers.name: Libya
answers.fact: Pentecost pilgrims came from the parts of Libya about Cyrene (Acts 2:10).

prompts.display_text: Pin a country Saints vol. 3 names among the nations at war by early August 1914.
prompts.text_original: Saints vol. 3 chapter 11 opens with German shells falling on Liege, Belgium, in August 1914, where a young Latter-day Saint named Arthur Horbach took cover. It names the nations already at war by early August. Pin a present-day country that matches one of those nations.
prompts.note: Austria-Hungary is scored as Austria and Hungary only; other lands it then ruled are not scored.
prompts.summary: After a Serbian nationalist killed the heir to Austria-Hungary in 1914, the empire went to war with Serbia, and their allies quickly followed. By early August, Serbia, Russia, France, Belgium and Great Britain faced Austria-Hungary and Germany. Saints tells the war's start through Arthur Horbach, a teenage member in Liege, Belgium.

answers.name: Germany
answers.fact: Named as fighting alongside Austria-Hungary.

answers.name: France
answers.fact: Named on the side of Serbia.

answers.name: United Kingdom
answers.fact: Great Britain is named on the side of Serbia.

answers.name: Russia
answers.fact: Named on the side of Serbia.

answers.name: Austria
answers.fact: Austria-Hungary, whose heir was assassinated, is named.

answers.name: Belgium
answers.fact: Named; Germany invaded France through Belgium, shelling Liege.

answers.name: Hungary
answers.fact: The other half of Austria-Hungary.

answers.name: Serbia
answers.fact: Austria-Hungary first went to war with the Kingdom of Serbia.
